desc: Reformulate fixed-distance feasibility as minimizing the number of upward edges over labels \(x_v\in[0,D]\), with \(x_1=0\), \(x_N=D\), and \(x_v\le x_u+1\) for every edge \(u\to v\).
Derive and verify an Ishikawa-style minimum-cut construction for the fixed target \(D\), including label conventions, implication arcs, edge-cost arcs, and terminal constraints.
Prove the equivalence between the fixed-\(D\) label optimum and the min-cut value, including parallel edges.
Establish binary-search bounds and monotonicity: target \(D\) is feasible exactly when the min-cut value is at most \(K\).
Analyze complexity and specify a suitable max-flow implementation for \(N\le30,M\le100\).
